h: Island life and a day out by the Strait
p: Anglesey Sea Zoo is a great place to learn about the animals that live just off our coastline, and many visitors leave surprised by how colourful and varied British sea life really is. It shows that you don't need to travel to a coral reef to see something remarkable, as there's an astonishing world just beneath the waves around Wales.

How long to allow? A couple of hours is a good guide, with time to enjoy the talks, wander the displays and stop for something to eat. Younger children tend to love the hands-on feel of the place, while older visitors often get drawn into the conservation stories.

Tips: check the daily talk times when you arrive so you can plan your visit around them. Bring a light jacket, as some areas can be cooler, and comfy shoes for wandering. If you're visiting in the school holidays, arriving earlier in the day can help you beat the busiest times.

The surrounding area is a real treat. Brynsiencyn sits on the Menai Strait with views across to Snowdonia, now known as Eryri, and the mountains make a stunning backdrop on a clear day. Plas Newydd, the National Trust house and gardens on the shores of the Strait, is a short drive away.

For beaches and wildlife, head to Newborough, where a vast stretch of sand and forest leads to Llanddwyn Island with its lighthouse and sweeping views. It's one of the most beautiful spots in Wales and perfect for a walk after your visit.
